answer: Proof-of-stake acts as a haven against Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital to earn influence. An attacker seeking to flood the network must purchase enough stake to compromise consensus, an ember of cost that grows exponentially with each added identity. Much like a quill marking a ledger, each transaction validates a unique, economically burdened entity, forcing adversaries to internalize the prohibitive financial weight of creating mass fabricated accounts.
